doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

chapter: Rutgers and the Institute of Jazz Studies
title: Library degree and the gamble on the Institute job
summary: He learned on the job, then earned a library science degree to succeed the retiring librarian.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. You were learning on the job.

Yeah exactly. And eventually I got a degree. I went down to New Brunswick’s library school and I got my degree in library science. And I was able to get the job that the librarian there had, before me. And in fact it was her — she in fact told me, “You should get the degree because I’m going to retire soon and you’ll probably be the perfect replacement, if you get your degree.” So I did. And I don’t recommend people get a degree just for one job. Because if I didn’t get that job I didn’t know what I would have done. Because I didn’t want to do anything else. I didn’t want to be a music librarian in

some other institution. I wanted to be in the Institute of Jazz Studies. I mean if I didn’t get that job I don’t know what I would have done. But that’s weird. It just worked out. But it was a gamble. It was a big gamble.
Well I can attest that it’s a pretty cool place.
